argument_summary: The certification defense should be read narrowly. Admissible evidence supports launch readiness in aggregate, absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents, and bounded deployment controls through a 7% initial rollout, rollback, and monitoring. The same admissible record also shows the clinical coding assistant observation-status weakness remains material and exposed, and that no approved risk acceptance covers it. The supportable position is therefore not clean present compliance; it is caveated certification logic that is defensible only if the packet is treated as requiring contemporaneous model-card disclosure of that limitation at launch.
claims_about_business_cost: No separate business-cost claim is needed to resolve the audit issue. The governance question can be handled by accurately scoping the certification basis and preserving monitoring and rollback as residual-risk controls rather than treating them as policy substitutes.
claims_about_policy: The policy cuts both ways and should be applied as written. It allows rollout and monitoring to mitigate residual deployment risk, but it also states they do not remove disclosure duties when the affected use case remains exposed unless approved risk acceptance covers that exposure. The admissible evidence does not support claiming that rollout controls substitute for disclosure, and it does not support claiming that approved risk acceptance already exists. It does support narrowing the actor position to a caveated basis: certification is supportable only with launch-time disclosure of the exposed limitation, not as unconditional compliance.
concessions: The admissible record shows a material weakness remains in the clinical coding assistant segment and that segment is still exposed in the initial cohort.
The current risk-acceptance document is only a draft, has no approver, and does not cover the exposed clinical coding assistant segment.
The present record does not prove that the required model-card disclosure artifact has already been finalized or approved for launch.
The actor should not be treated as claiming clean compliance on the current record.
